description:
Rule: a test learns that something happened from a message or a telemetry event, never by waiting on a clock and never by polling.

Trigger: on 2026-11-13, during a workspace gate run on a loaded machine, the oracle check ran real elixir on fixtures/00691_a_child_and_its_parent_both_time_out_in_order.oracle.exs and elixir itself printed :main_timeout before :child_timeout. The child times out after 20 ms and the parent after 80 ms; the order rests on the child being spawned, scheduled and printing inside the 60 ms gap. fz was not involved; three re-runs alone passed.

Census on 2053b04a5 (grep, not yet classified one by one):
- 16 fixtures use a non-zero receive `after` timeout: 00247, 00515, 00686, 00687, 00688, 00690, 00691, 00692, 00693, 00905, 01065, and fixtures2/behavior guard_plan_inputs, list_retention_receive_capture, map_key_unreached, receive_selective_refs, receive_outcome_identity. No fixture calls Process.sleep or :timer.sleep.
- Rust tests that sleep: src/aot_link_test.rs:167 (10 ms), src/telemetry/bus_test.rs:230, 255, 428, src/telemetry/jsonl_test.rs:295, src/telemetry/sink_test.rs:341 (50 us each).

For each one, decide which it is:
1. The timeout is not the point (it stands in for "nothing else arrives"): use `after 0`, and fix any order between processes with a message.
2. The timeout firing is the point, but only one process is involved: a single timeout has no race; keep the smallest value.
3. An order between two timers or between a timer and another process is the point (00691, 00693, 00690, 00692): the order must not rest on a margin. Sequence with messages where Elixir can express the same thing; where the fact under test is the runtime timer order itself, assert it from telemetry (timer armed with its deadline, timer fired) in a Rust test, and keep the oracle fixture to what a message can order.
4. Rust sleeps: replace each with the event the test is actually waiting for.

Done when: every item above is classified in this ticket with what replaced it, no fixture output depends on a timing margin, no Rust test sleeps, and the suites are green on interp, run and build.
title: No fixture or test gets its answer from a wall-clock wait
